reports.title: UK Electricity Mix Weekly Report: Friday 14 August
reports.intro: A measured weekly report for EnergyMix.info using the available 7-day historical generation feed for Saturday 8 August to Thursday 13 August.
reports.summary: The week from Saturday 8 August to Thursday 13 August averaged about 23.6 GW of measured generation, with renewables averaging 42.8% of measured output. The strongest renewable day in the available data was Saturday 8 August, when wind, solar and hydro together averaged 51.4% of measured generation. Gas was highest on Thursday 13 August and lowest on Saturday 8 August.
reports.takeaway: For flexible electricity use, the cleanest opportunities are likely to appear when wind is strong, gas is low and demand is not at a peak. This is the foundation for future EV-charging guidance, clean-electricity alerts and weekly newsletter summaries.
drivers: Renewables were strongest on Saturday 8 August, when wind, solar and hydro averaged 51.4% of measured generation.
Wind was the largest swing factor in the available feed, peaking at about 6.7 GW average output on Saturday 8 August.
Solar was strongest on Tuesday 11 August, averaging about 4.9 GW across settlement periods after embedded-solar backfill where needed.
Gas averaged about 7.0 GW across the period, rising highest on Thursday 13 August and falling lowest on Saturday 8 August.
Measured generation was highest on Wednesday 12 August, at roughly 26.0 GW average output.

cleanestPeriods.title: Best low-carbon proxy: Saturday 8 August
cleanestPeriods.body: Historical carbon-intensity aggregates are not yet part of this weekly report feed, so EnergyMix.info uses renewable share and gas output as cautious proxies. Saturday 8 August had the strongest renewable share at 51.4%.

cleanestPeriods.title: Lowest gas proxy: Saturday 8 August
cleanestPeriods.body: Gas generation averaged about 4.5 GW on Saturday 8 August. Lower gas periods are often cleaner, but the report does not yet claim this was the lowest-carbon period without historical carbon-intensity validation.

higherCarbonPeriods.title: Highest gas proxy: Thursday 13 August
higherCarbonPeriods.body: Gas averaged about 11.7 GW on Thursday 13 August. Gas-heavy periods are usually higher-carbon, but this is labelled as a proxy until historical carbon-intensity highs/lows are added to the report feed.

socialPosts.title: Monday weekly grid brief
socialPosts.body:
Last week in Britain’s electricity mix:

• Highest renewable share in the available feed: 51.4% on Saturday 8 August
• Highest average wind output: ~6.7 GW on Saturday 8 August
• Highest average solar output: ~4.9 GW on Tuesday 11 August
• Highest average gas output: ~11.7 GW on Thursday 13 August

The shift was clear: gas-heavy weekdays gave way to a cleaner, wind-led weekend.

Full report: https://energymix.info/reports/weekly/2026-08-14/

socialPosts.title: Wednesday explainer
socialPosts.body:
What does “UK electricity mix” actually mean?

For live grid dashboards, it usually means Great Britain’s electricity system: England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is part of the UK, but operates in a separate electricity market.

Explainer: https://energymix.info/uk-electricity-mix

socialPosts.title: Friday practical clean-electricity post
socialPosts.body:
The cleanest time to use electricity is not a fixed hour.

It changes with wind, solar, demand, imports and gas generation. Windy overnight periods and sunny middays can be much cleaner than still early-evening peaks.

Guide: https://energymix.info/cleanest-time-to-use-electricity
